name: South Sudan
summary_text: South Sudan is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. The 2008 Penal Code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 14 years), and Human Dignity Trust lists South Sudan as criminalising the gender expression of trans people. The country has barely emerged from civil war, state institutions are vestigial outside Juba, communal violence is endemic, and there is no documented LGBT community infrastructure whatsoever — no organisation can operate openly. No trans-specific case is documented because documentation itself is nearly impossible. For a visitor: statutory risk plus a near-total absence of protective institutions.
